newsitem.title: USA: Dana sees Eaton unit purchase accretive.
newsitem.headline: Dana sees Eaton unit purchase accretive.

text.p: Dana Corp's Chief Financial Officer Jack Simpson said the company expects the acquisition of Eaton Corp's global axle and brake operations to be accretive to earnings per share in 1998.
"We do see it being accretive to EPS in '98," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

In announcements made earlier on Wednesday, the two companies said they had reached agreements under which Dana would buy Eaton's axle and brake operations for $287 million and Eaton would buy Dana's worldwide vehicular clutch business for $180 million. Both sales are cash deals.
Dana said in a press statement that it saw an after-tax gain of about $70 million, or $0.67 per share, from the sale of its clutch unit.
Simpson that subject to regulatory approvals and the completion of due diligence, the deals could close in the third quarter.
He also said that he is comfortable with analysts' earnings per share estimates of $3.17 to $3.27 for 1997. "We're comfortable with that, even with the effects of the strikes."
The company, as a supplier to Chrysler Corp, has been hurt by strikes earlier this year at the automaker's engine plant.

Simpson said that the divestiture of the clutch business was part of the company's ongoing process to focus on core operations. He said that other disposals may be announced "shortly" but declined to name them.
In April this year, Dana said it was selling its global hydraulic cylinder manufacturing operations.

Simpson said it was too early to say if the company would be taking any charges related to Wednesday's agreements. "It's too soon to tell if there will be any (charges)," he said. "There may be some charges we could be looking at...when we've completed due diligence".
Sales at the clutch facilities Dana is selling are estimated at $179 million for 1997, and sales at Eaton's axle and brake unit are estimated at $625 million, according to Dana's press release.
Shares of Dana were up 3/16 to 38 in late morning trading. Shares of Eaton were up 7/16 to 86-1/2.
